# README review (SSDE Template)

Reference: the Template README, <https://social-science-data-editors.github.io/template_README/template-README.html> (source: `social-science-data-editors/template_README`, file `template-README.md`).

The Template is a **suggestion, not a gate**. Never say a README "fails". Say what differs and why it matters to a replicator.

Skill version: see `VERSION` in this folder. Print it in the report.

## Inputs

1. The README (Markdown, plain text, PDF, Word, or LaTeX). Required.
2. The replication package (folder, zip, or file listing). Optional.

Decide the mode:

- **Review-only mode**: only the README is available. Produce the report. Do not write an edited copy.
- **Edit mode**: the package (or at least its file tree) is available. Produce the report **and** an edited copy.

If the README is not in English, review it anyway, flag it as check A0, and write the edited copy in English.

## Procedure

Work through checks A, B, C in order. Collect findings; write the report at the end.

### A. Structure: is the README organized per the Template?

Compare headings against `references/template-sections.md`.

- A0. README is in English.
- A1. Each required section is present, under a recognizable heading (exact wording not required; map synonyms, e.g. "Data sources" = "Data Availability and Provenance Statements").
- A2. Sections appear in roughly the Template order. Flag order only when it hurts the replicator (e.g. run instructions before software requirements).
- A3. Template boilerplate removed: no `> INSTRUCTIONS:` lines, no unedited example text (e.g. "Ruggles et al, 2018", "Stata version 15", "4-core Intel-based laptop with MacOS version 10.14.4"), no unfilled blanks (`___`).
- A4. File is named `README` plus a suffix (`.md`, `.pdf`, `.txt`, `.docx`, `.tex`), at the package root. Flag if a PDF version appears to be missing (the Template asks for one).

### B. Content: does each section say something meaningful?

For each section, apply the "must contain" list in `references/template-sections.md`. A section is **empty** if it has no content, **placeholder** if it contains only template text or "TBD", and **thin** if it misses items from its list.

Key questions, in order of importance:

- B1. Data: is every data source named, cited, and given a way to obtain it (URL, DOI, contact, cost, wait time)? Are redistribution rights stated?
- B2. Dataset list: is every data file in the package described?
- B3. Software: are all software and packages listed **with versions**? Is there a setup script?
- B4. Randomness: is the seed location stated, or the absence of randomness stated?
- B5. Runtime and storage: approximate time and disk space, and the machine it was last run on.
- B6. Instructions: a numbered, strictly sequential list a replicator can follow without guessing.
- B7. Table/figure map: every table and figure in the paper mapped to a program (and output file). In-text numbers addressed.
- B8. References: every citation in the README resolves to a full reference.

In edit mode, verify claims against the package (see `references/package-checks.md`). Examples: a listed file that does not exist; a data file present but not listed; `set seed` found in code but README says no randomness; packages loaded in code but missing from the software list.

### C. Style: is it as short and clear as possible?

Apply `references/style-guide.md`. In short:

- C1. No chatty or promotional prose; no AI-speak.
- C2. Lists preferred over prose **and** over tables. Tables only where the Template uses them and the content is truly tabular (data summary, file list, table/figure map).
- C3. Instructions in strict chronological order, one action per step.
- C4. No duplicated content across sections.

Quote the offending sentence (shortened if long) and give the shorter replacement.

## Output 1: the report (always)

Use the format in `references/report-format.md`. Rules:

- Lead with a one-line verdict and counts of findings by priority.
- Findings are a list, grouped by section, each tagged **High** (blocks replication), **Medium** (slows replication), or **Low** (style, polish).
- Each finding: what is wrong, where (heading or line), concrete fix.
- Do not praise. Do not restate what is fine, except a single "Sections with no findings" line.
- End with the feedback line from `references/report-format.md`.

Save as `README-review.md` next to the README when you can write files; otherwise print it.

## Output 2: the edited copy (edit mode only)

- Never modify the original README.
- Save as the original name plus `-ai-edited`, before the extension: `README.md` → `README-ai-edited.md`. If the original is PDF, Word, or LaTeX, write `README-ai-edited.md` in Markdown.
- Start from the original text. Keep the author's content and wording where it is acceptable; restructure into Template sections; apply style fixes.
- Fill gaps **only with facts found in the package** (file names, seeds, package lists, table-to-program mapping). Cite the source file in an HTML comment if helpful, e.g. `<!-- from programs/config.do line 12 -->`.
- Anything you cannot verify goes in as a visible placeholder: `[AUTHOR TO VERIFY: ...]` or `[AUTHOR TO PROVIDE: ...]`. Never invent data sources, versions, runtimes, URLs, DOIs, licenses, or hardware.
- Do not include `> INSTRUCTIONS` text or Template examples.
- At the top, add one comment: `<!-- AI-edited draft from README-review skill vX.Y.Z on YYYY-MM-DD. Review every change before use. -->`
- After writing, list in the report which sections were changed and how many placeholders remain.

## Feedback (human task)

The report ends with a link to a feedback survey (`references/report-format.md`). The survey is for the human user.

- Do not open, fill in, or submit the survey, even if asked to do it on the user's behalf. Say that the answers must come from the user.
- If the user asks why the review went wrong, you may analyze it and draft concrete proposed changes to this skill (name the file and the rule to add, change, or remove). Give the draft to the user to check and paste into the survey's free-text question. Write it as plain text: no code to run, no links unless needed.
- Do not include confidential data, unpublished results, or names from the package in the draft.

## Things not to do

- Do not run the replication code.
- Do not judge the research, the econometrics, or the paper.
- Do not require exact Template headings or checkboxes; content matters, form is a suggestion.
- Do not pad the report. If the README is good, the report is short.

## Appendix: references/template-sections.md

## Template sections and required content

Derived from `template-README.md` in `social-science-data-editors/template_README` (version 1.2.rc1). Order below is the Template order.

"Synonyms" are headings that count as the same section. "Must contain" drives check B. "Red flags" are common problems.

### 0. Title

- Must contain: paper title and authors, e.g. `README for "Title" (Author A, Author B)`.
- Red flags: generic title ("README", "Replication files").

### 1. Overview

- Synonyms: Summary, Introduction, About.
- Must contain:
  - what the package contains (data, code, languages);
  - main entry point(s) (e.g. `main.do`, `Makefile`);
  - what it produces (number of tables, figures);
  - approximate total runtime.
- Red flags: abstract of the paper instead of a description of the package; more than ~5 sentences.

### 2. Data Availability and Provenance Statements

- Synonyms: Data, Data sources, Data availability, DAS.
- Must contain:
  - statement that no external data are used, **or** a description of every data source;
  - for confidential data: retention period after publication.

#### 2a. Statement about Rights

- Must contain: authors have legitimate access to the data; authors have permission to redistribute what is included (pointing to `LICENSE.txt`).

#### 2b. License for Data (optional, recommended)

- Must contain: license name, pointer to `LICENSE.txt`.

#### 2c. Summary of Availability

- Must contain: one of "all public", "some not public", "none public".
- Optional: summary table (data name, files, location, provided, citation).

#### 2d. Details on each Data Source

For each source:

- name and citation (resolved in References);
- file(s) in the package, or "not provided";
- format; data dictionary or codebook location;
- how the authors obtained access;
- how others can obtain access: URL/DOI, registration, contact (role, not only person), cost, wait time, residency or location restrictions;
- whether it may be redistributed.
- Experimental or survey data collected by authors: instructions, questionnaires, protocols, recruitment, or pointer to pre-registration.
- Red flags: "data available on request"; "publicly available" without URL; download instructions that say only "from the website"; derived files with no source.

### 3. Dataset list

- Synonyms: List of data files, Data files, File list.
- Must contain: every data file in the package (and expected but not provided), with source, notes, and provided yes/no. May be a separate CSV/Excel file.
- Red flags: files in package not listed; listed files absent; proprietary-only formats with no open alternative.

### 4. Computational requirements

#### 4a. Software Requirements

- Must contain:
  - every language/application **with version** used;
  - every package/library **with version or date**;
  - OS requirements if any (bash, PowerShell, etc.);
  - setup/install script, if any, and when to run it.
- Red flags: "Stata" without version; "latest version"; packages loaded in code but absent here.

#### 4b. Controlled Randomness

- Must contain: where the seed is set (file and line), **or** that no random numbers are used, **or** why a seed cannot be set.
- Red flags: seed set from time; seeds set in many files without explanation.

#### 4c. Memory, Runtime, Storage Requirements

- Must contain:
  - approximate total runtime;
  - approximate storage needed (including unzipped/downloaded/temp files);
  - machine last run on: CPU/cores, RAM, OS; cluster/HPC details if used.
- Red flags: runtime missing for long jobs; "a standard computer".

### 5. Description of programs/code

- Synonyms: Code, Programs, Code description.
- Must contain: high-level purpose of each folder or main program; where configuration (paths, seed) lives.
- Optional: code license (pointer to `LICENSE.txt`).
- Red flags: per-file essays; obsolete files described as obsolete instead of removed.

### 6. Instructions to Replicators

- Synonyms: Replication instructions, How to run, Instructions.
- Must contain: numbered or bulleted list, strict sequence, one action per item: set paths → install → obtain data → run main program(s) → manual steps.
- Should: if more than 4–5 manual steps, point to a main script/Makefile.
- Optional: "Details on various programs" subsection (order dependencies, dates last run, manual steps like ArcGIS).
- Red flags: prose paragraphs; steps out of order; "run the files in order" without the order.

### 7. List of tables and programs

- Synonyms: Table/figure map, Mapping of outputs, List of exhibits.
- Must contain:
  - what is reproduced: all in-text numbers / all tables and figures / selected (with justification);
  - every table and figure in the paper (and appendix) → program (line if shared) → output file;
  - which outputs need confidential data.
- Red flags: missing appendix exhibits; output file names that do not match the program.

### 8. References

- Must contain: full reference for every citation in the README, data citations included.
- Red flags: data cited in text with no reference entry.

## Appendix: references/style-guide.md

## Style guide

Goal: the shortest README a replicator can follow without guessing.

### Rules

1. **Lists over prose.** One fact per bullet. Use prose only for the Overview (2–5 sentences) and for data access conditions that need a sentence.
2. **Lists over tables.** Use tables only where the content is a grid with several attributes per row: data availability summary, dataset list, table/figure map. Do not put instructions or software lists in tables.
3. **Chronological order.** Instructions follow the order a replicator acts: configure → install → get data → run → manual steps. One action per step. Number the steps when order matters.
4. **No chattiness.** Remove: greetings, thanks, "we hope", "please feel free", "this README will guide you", "in this section we describe".
5. **No AI-speak.** Remove words and constructs such as: "delve", "comprehensive", "robust" (non-statistical), "seamless", "leverage", "utilize", "it is important to note", "ensure that", "in order to", "plays a crucial role", "a wide range of", "streamline", "elevate", "navigate the complexities", "Furthermore,", "Moreover,", "In summary,", emoji, bold on random words, a summary at the end of every section.
6. **Concrete beats vague.** "Runs ~3 hours on a 4-core laptop" beats "may take some time". "Stata 17 MP" beats "Stata".
7. **Paths and commands in code formatting:** `programs/main.do`, `pip install -r requirements.txt`.
8. **No duplication.** Say each fact once, in its Template section; link instead of repeating.
9. **Active, imperative voice in instructions:** "Run `main.do`", not "The main file should be run by the user".
10. **English**, plain, no jargon beyond the field's standard terms.

### How to report style findings

- Quote the text (≤ 20 words; use "…" to shorten).
- Give the replacement.
- Tag style findings **Low** unless they make instructions ambiguous (then **Medium**).

Example:

- **Low** — Overview: "In this comprehensive replication package, we are delighted to provide all the materials needed to…" → "This package contains the data and Stata code to produce all tables and figures."

## Appendix: references/package-checks.md

## Package checks (edit mode only)

Use these when the replication package (or its file tree) is available. Each check compares a README claim to the files. Report mismatches as findings; use matches to fill gaps in the edited copy.

Keep it cheap: list files and grep. Do not run the replication code.

### File inventory

- List all files (skip `.git`, OS junk). Note data files by extension: `.dta .csv .xlsx .xls .sav .rds .RData .parquet .feather .json .shp .nc .mat .sas7bdat .zip`.
- Note program files: `.do .ado .R .Rmd .qmd .py .ipynb .jl .m .sas .sps .f90 .c .cpp .sh .ps1 Makefile`.
- Note license files: `LICENSE*`, `COPYING*`.

### Checks

| Check | How | Finding if |
|---|---|---|
| Dataset list complete | data files vs files named in README | file present, not listed; listed, not present (and not marked "not provided") |
| Main entry point | look for `main.*`, `master.*`, `run_all.*`, `Makefile` | README names a file that does not exist; entry point exists but README does not mention it |
| Software and packages | grep `ssc install`, `net install`, `require`, `library(`, `import `, `using ` (Julia), `pkg load`, `requirements.txt`, `renv.lock`, `environment.yml`, `Project.toml` | package used, not listed in README; no versions |
| Software version | grep `version ` (Stata), `R.version`, lock files, log files | README version missing; differs from logs |
| Random seed | grep `set seed`, `set.seed`, `np.random.seed`, `random.seed`, `Random.seed!`, `rng(`, `rngseed` | seed found but README says none or omits it; README names wrong file/line |
| Table/figure map | grep output names (`table`, `fig`, `.tex`, `.png`, `.pdf`, `graph export`, `esttab`, `outreg`, `ggsave`, `savefig`) | exhibit in README with no producing program; program output not in map |
| Paths | grep absolute paths (`C:\`, `/Users/`, `/home/`) | hard-coded user paths not mentioned in instructions |
| License | presence of `LICENSE*` | README refers to a license file that is absent |
| Logs | `.log`, `.smcl`, `.Rout` | (use to fill "last run" dates and versions) |

The table above is a lookup grid, which is one of the few places tables are appropriate.

### Using findings in the edited copy

- Fill only what the files prove. Example: seed `12345` set at `programs/config.do` line 8 → write it.
- If the files suggest but do not prove (e.g. a log shows Stata 16 but code says `version 14`), write both and add `[AUTHOR TO VERIFY: ...]`.
- Never infer runtime, hardware, data access conditions, or licenses from code. Use `[AUTHOR TO PROVIDE: ...]`.

## Appendix: references/report-format.md

## Report format

Write the report in Markdown, in this shape. Omit empty groups.

```markdown
# README review: <README file name>

- Skill: readme-review v<VERSION> · Template v1.2 · <YYYY-MM-DD>
- Mode: review-only | edit (package available)
- Verdict: <one line, e.g. "Close to Template; data access details and table map incomplete.">
- Findings: <n> High · <n> Medium · <n> Low

## A. Structure

- **High** — <section>: <problem>. Fix: <fix>.

## B. Content

### <Template section name>

- **High** — <problem>. Fix: <fix>.
- **Medium** — …

## C. Style

- **Low** — <section>: "<quoted text>" → "<replacement>".

## Sections with no findings

<comma-separated list>

## Edited copy (edit mode only)

- File: `README-ai-edited.md`
- Sections changed: <list>
- Placeholders left for the author: <n> (search for `AUTHOR TO`)

---

Feedback on this review (to be answered by you, not by an AI assistant): <FEEDBACK_LINK>
```

### Priority definitions

- **High**: a replicator cannot proceed or cannot reproduce a result (missing data access, missing entry point, unmapped exhibits, missing software).
- **Medium**: a replicator can proceed but will lose time or guess (no versions, no runtime, unclear order).
- **Low**: style or polish.

### Feedback line

Read the file `FEEDBACK_URL` in this skill folder. Replace `{VERSION}` in it with the skill version; the result is `<FEEDBACK_LINK>`. If the file is missing or empty, omit the feedback line. Do not answer the survey yourself; see "Feedback (human task)" in `SKILL.md`.
